candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16
candidate.educational_objective: State the routine antepartum and postpartum timing of Rho(D) immune globulin.

options.A: It is routinely given at 26–28 weeks of gestation and again after delivery if the newborn is Rh-positive.
options.B: It is given only after delivery and never during pregnancy.
options.C: It is given only during the first trimester.
options.D: It is routinely given after delivery only when the newborn is Rh-negative.

candidate.rationale: Rho(D) immune globulin labeling recommends antepartum prophylaxis at 26–28 weeks for appropriate unsensitized Rh-negative pregnant clients. A postpartum dose is indicated when the newborn is Rh-positive.
candidate.source_claim_supported: RhoGAM is given at 26–28 weeks for routine antepartum prophylaxis and postpartum when the newborn is Rh-positive.
candidate.source_locator: Dosage and Administration—Antepartum prophylaxis at 26–28 weeks; Postpartum if newborn is Rh-positive
candidate.stem: An unsensitized Rh-negative pregnant client asks when Rho(D) immune globulin is routinely given. Which response is correct?
